title: AI Copilots for Tech Architecture: The Highest-ROI Use Case You’re Not Building — Boris B., Catio
talk_summary: A vendor pitch from Catio for an 'architecture co-pilot' that ingests cloud/K8s/log data into a live 'digital twin' of the tech estate, then uses multi-agent LLM systems to produce ROI-ranked, explainable architecture recommendations and conversational design guidance.

takeaways.technique: Living system model as agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: They ingest data across clouds, Kubernetes, and logging into a normalized 'digital twin' that reflects reality rather than the wiki, and feed that as context to agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a true system model that reflects the reality not what's in your wiki or not it's what you have as opposed to what you think you have

takeaways.what_they_do: Architecture standards and governance are embedded in the agent's context so generated designs are compliant by default rather than caught in periodic review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whatever designs are given actually follow this guidance intrinsically

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the review role shifts from checking whether standards were met to knowing they were met by construction, freeing reviewers for strategy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: change the review role from being, you know, kind of trying to figure out if standards are being met to knowing the standards are met by by design

takeaways.what_they_do: They frame architecture analysis as distributed problem solving: agents each own a slice of the dependency graph and collaborate to a global recommendation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to break out all the dependencies and then attack them and then and then work together to actually come up to some kind of recommendation that is global in context

takeaways.technique: Start small, prove ROI, then scale
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend piloting on one portfolio area, tying to specific business outcomes, and scaling only after ROI is proven.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start small tie to business outcomes to specific business outcomes in that area and then start piloting some autonomous guidance with one team
